sources.title: Yuri Bregel: Central Asia vii, In the Eighteenth to Nineteenth Centuries
sources.note: Direct article read, three dynasties, administrative differences and Russian conquest. Avoids dated value judgments about enlightenment and simplistic ethnic categories. Atlas caveats derive from identity.json, not from this article.

sources.title: Timur Beisembiev and Scott Levi: Kokand Khanate
sources.note: Direct article read, sections Initial stage, Period of expansion, and Socio-political crisis. Uses 1709 emergence, eighteenth-century migration, 1810s canals, 1815-16 Shahrikhan, Qing relations and 1876 annexation.

sources.title: Evelin Grassi: Delshad Barna, educator, historian and poet
sources.note: Direct article read, paragraphs 1-6 and manuscript bibliography. Her autobiography is the chief source for captivity and family education. Avoids incompatible-looking annual and lifetime pupil counts; no unsupported court-poet appointment.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Bridle, Mane piece and Breast collar, 16.136a-c
sources.note: Direct collection metadata read. Nineteenth century, Uzbek/Kokand Khanate; leather, silver, turquoise, carnelian, enamel, textile. Owner and precise manufacture date unknown.

sources.title: Eugene Schuyler: Turkistan, volume II (1876), page 10
sources.note: Direct full PDF open failed. Indexed original Library of Congress PDF returned complete printed page 10 with query: "04024471v2" "palace". Eyewitness 1873 journey: glazed palace facade, brief external view, mint workers making harness ornaments, mint master as court jeweller. Does not adopt superlatives or infer unseen interiors.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Samarkand tea stalls, photograph dated 1865-1872
sources.note: Direct catalogue read, title translation, date, summary and Turkestan Album plate 144/no.444. Uses catalogued description only; date spans Russian conquest, so presented as transition-era evidence.

sources.title: ICOMOS: Historic Centre of Bukhara evaluation, nomination 602
sources.note: Direct PDF read, printed page 72/PDF index1. Uses only 1848 sixteen public baths and Manghit ending in1920. Ancient chronology and loose 1868 incorporation wording in this old evaluation are excluded. Runtime Bukhara reuse counted cumulatively.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Bukhara Cover, early nineteenth century, 21.114.3
sources.note: Direct collection page read; suzani dowry, separate strips assigned to relatives, rejoined after embroidery. General process linked to an attributed early nineteenth-century Bukhara object. Runtime Bukhara reuse counted cumulatively.

sources.title: Charles C. Torrey: Gold Coins of Khokand and Bukhara (1950), catalogue no.12
sources.note: Direct ANS open blocked; indexed original full catalogue returned exact Arabic-script phrase with query site:numismatics.org/digitallibrary/ark "Gold Coins" "ضرب بخارا". No.12 specifies Nasr Allah, Bukhara, AH1257 and 4.55g. Same-work Pahar scan text confirms printed pp.35-36/PDF indices40-41; web screenshot unavailable. Quoted specimen is modern editorial transcription, not a claimed new reading of coin photograph. Runtime Bukhara reuse counted.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth: Chorasmia ii, In Islamic Times
sources.note: Indexed original article read, final historical paragraph: 1873 invasion and truncated protectorate, Abd Allah loss of throne in February1920. Runtime Khiva reuse counted cumulatively.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Itchan Kala, Khiva domestic architecture
sources.note: Direct institutional page read, Outstanding Universal Value, domestic architecture paragraph. Courtyard, reception portico, carved posts and private apartments; surviving variants span eighteenth to twentieth centuries. No assumption every house dates before1914. Runtime Khiva reuse counted cumulatively.

proposedOverrides.name: Central Asian khanates
proposedOverrides.summary: Separate oasis and pastoral states, including Bukhara, Khiva and Kokand; imported outlines are unreliable.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: New regional narrative only. No shared alias with any individual khanate and no new map identities.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: Broad imported label interpreted as a comparative regional account of separate Bukhara, Khiva and eighteenth-century-onward Kokand. This is an explicit editorial scope, not validation that every polygon depicts those states.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Severe unresolved atlas defects:1530 polygon bbox54.0167E73.3569N68.9353E76.9273N in Arctic;1600 outline reaches164.923E77.592N;1783 records combine Central Asian and Caucasian pieces;1878-1900 only Pamir outline;1900-1914 composite. Public opening and summary warn unreliable boundaries. All decoded features in identity.json; no geometry edited or certified.
batchIdentityNotes.existingRelated: Runtime khiva-khanate and shared bokhara-khanate/bukara-khanate already have detailed narrower narratives. quazaq-khanate and chagatai-khanate are separate. No aliases absorbed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: 1530 is atlas start, not the founding of every state. Kokand emerges1709 and ends1876. Russian domination did not immediately abolish Bukhara or Khiva; both monarchies ended1920, beyond this record.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No population homogenization or exact claim to all Central Asia; no inferred medical treatments or toilet design. The bath evidence concerns1848 Bukhara. Photograph1865-1872 and Khiva surviving houses into20th century are explicitly dated regional context.
